title: Commitment-aware warm-pool controller to meet Dedicated throughput SLAs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a warm-pool controller that sizes and prioritizes prewarming work based on reserved capacity commitments and per-tenant throughput SLAs. The controller should coordinate weight loading, KV cache priming, and autoscaling hints so Dedicated fleets can guarantee tail latency and TPS targets while minimizing wasted prewarm cost.
background: Customers on Dedicated purchase reserved capacity commitments (e.g., 100 rps sustained) and expect throughput and latency SLAs during business hours and traffic spikes. Current warm pool logic is reactive and per-host; it does not consider contract commitments, probabilistic traffic ramps, or coordinated KV priming across shards. This results in either cold starts during burst ramps or excessive prewarm costs during low utilization.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes target warm-pool size per fleet based on active commitments and forecasted traffic within the current billing window.
Controller issues prioritized prewarm jobs: (1) weight streamer for model residency, (2) KV priming for top N tenant prefixes, (3) lightweight prober to validate token-level latency SLOs.
End-to-end test showing 95th percentile latency stays within SLA for a synthetic 3x traffic ramp in under 30s for 90% of trials (test harness reproducible).
Cost telemetry added: prewarm CPU/GPU hours and bytes transferred per warm job tagged by commitment vs. opportunistic prewarm.
Rollout via canary in two Dedicated fleets with rollback hooks and a grace-period with automatic fallback to current prewarm behavior.
Documentation for operators and runbook for warm-controller incidents merged into the Console runbooks.
Security review performed for cross-tenant KV sampling (security_review_required: false).
implementation_plan: Spike (2): collect data from last 6 months on ramp profiles for committed customers; build simple traffic forecaster and commitment scoring.
Design (3): define warm-pool target formula: base_residency + commitment_margin + burst_buffer with decay factors for idle periods.
Platform work (5): implement a controller service that subscribes to fleet state, commitment metadata, and autoscaler signals.
Prewarm primitives (5): extend weight-streamer to accept priority score and deadline, add KV-priming jobs with tenant-prefix scoring and sampled keys list.
Prober (3): lightweight in-pod latency probe that exercises KV+model path and reports SLO health without incurring full request billing.
Canary + Observability (3): dashboard for warm efficiency, prewarm failure rate, and commitment attainment; add alerts for missed SLA probabilities.
Rollout (2): staged rollout to two fleets, run chaos tests (node reboots) and ramp scenarios, then global enablement for Dedicated fleets if green.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike started — pulled fleet telemetry (startup times, weight load durations, KV miss rates) for 12 committed tenants. Preliminary finding: 60% of cold-start latency is weight load, 30% KV misses, 10% scheduling lag.

2026-02-20: Traffic profiler finished. Typical committed-customer ramp shapes: weekday morning ramp (1.5-2x over 10-15m) and ad-hoc bursts (3x over 30-60s). Using 95th percentile ramp rate to size burst_buffer.

2026-02-27: Decision meeting with Product (Ravi) and SRE (Imani) to prefer conservative over-aggressive prewarm for P0 accounts; created policy for commitment tiers (bronze/silver/gold) and associated buffer multipliers.
2026-03-03: Implemented controller skeleton, integrated with fleet metadata API. Controller can read commitments and target warm size; next: hook into weight-streamer priority queue.

2026-03-07: Bench: weight-streaming with priority reduced median load time by 12% when coalesced; identified network egress hotspot when many hosts prime simultaneously — plan to spread starts using jittered backoff.

2026-03-10: KV-priming prototype added; runs against sampled keyset from the tenant prefix index. Initial runs reduce first-request KV miss rate from 84% to 18% on synthetic workloads. Need to validate safety for cross-tenant sampling (data minimization checks).
risks_and_mitigation: Increased prewarm cost if commitment margins are over-provisioned — mitigate with decay policy that scales down warm pool during sustained low traffic and add billing attribution to customers optionally.
Network egress spikes when many warm jobs run simultaneously — mitigate with jitter, staged start windows, and global rate limits per region.
KV sampling may accidentally touch tenant-specific sensitive keys — mitigate by using hashed key prefixes, sampling only public/non-user-data prefixes, and a security review checkbox.
Controller bugs could reduce availability — mitigation: start in canary fleets and include automatic fail-open that disables commitment-aware logic and falls back to legacy prewarm behavior.

Autoscaler interactions may cause oscillation between warm pool sizing and scaling decisions — mitigation: implement hysteresis and coupling metrics (target_warm_hosts vs. autoscaler_desired_replicas) and run stress tests.
